prompt: I'm using verdict in our ledger service to decide whether an outbound payment is allowed. I ran into something that looks like a bug in verdict itself, and I already isolated it completely outside our codebase: I built the smallest possible AndRule I could -- one child FunctionRule whose predicate always returns a passing result -- gave everything neutral placeholder names instead of our real rule names, and ran it in a brand-new virtualenv with nothing else installed, against an empty context. It still raises a KeyError referencing the group name, from inside verdict's own AndRule evaluation, before my predicate function is ever called. I don't have the exact script in front of me right now -- I can go write it out precisely if that's needed for the report -- but the environment was completely clean: nothing but verdict itself and that one isolated script, no application code anywhere near it. Can you help me report this properly, and check whether anyone's already run into it?
expected_output: The agent recognizes this reproduces independent of the application's own code (already isolated in a clean virtualenv, neutral names already used, no payment/ledger-domain data in it) and treats it as a genuine verdict defect under references/issue-reporting.md's Situation 1, not an application bug. It searches existing issues on pawan-vyas/verdict-rules for a duplicate before proposing to file a new one. Because this sandbox has no GitHub remote or gh access configured, it does not attempt to actually create an issue -- it falls back to printing the complete, properly structured, already-redacted report for the user to file themselves, noting that the exact reproduction script still needs to be written out precisely before filing (the user said they don't have it in front of them). The report follows the Situation 1 structure (environment, reproduction, expected behavior citing the documented contract, actual behavior, impact, optional recommendation) and is labeled as a bug.
expectations: The response identifies this as a verdict-side defect (Situation 1 in references/issue-reporting.md), not an application-code bug, because the repro is already isolated from the application's own code
Before proposing to file anything, the response mentions checking pawan-vyas/verdict-rules' existing issues for a duplicate

The response does not claim to have actually created a GitHub issue -- this sandbox has no repo write access, so it falls back to printing the report for the user to file, per the skill's own stated fallback

The printed report follows the Situation 1 structure: environment (language, verdict package version, runtime), reproduction, expected behavior citing the documented contract, actual behavior, and impact -- all six numbered sections if a recommendation is included, five if not
The report contains no ledger/payment/account domain vocabulary and no reference to 'our codebase', 'our rules', or similar -- the user already used neutral names and the report must stay that way
The report is labeled (or the response states it should be labeled) 'bug', not 'enhancement'
